readingInstruction: Read Deuteronomy 26:1-28:14. This reading covers the firstfruits offering, a covenant ceremony at Ebal and Gerizim, and the first part of the great blessings and curses. Read the confession in 26:5-10 aloud as a creed.
settingTheScene: The long section of laws comes to an end with a ritual and a ceremony. In chapter 26, Moses describes the firstfruits offering that Israelites are to bring when they enter the land, including a short statement of faith to be recited. In chapter 27, he commands the people to set up large stones when they cross the Jordan and to pronounce blessings and curses at Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal. Chapter 28 begins the blessings and curses themselves, and you read the blessings first.
observation: The Israelite is to bring the firstfruits to the place that the LORD chooses and say, “A wandering Aramean was my father” (26:1-5).
The creed tells the story: Egypt, affliction, the cry to the LORD, the exodus, the land, and the firstfruits (26:5-10).
“And you shall rejoice in all the good that the LORD your God has given to you” (26:11).

This day the LORD your God commands you to do these statutes… “You have declared today that the LORD is your God… and the LORD has declared today that you are a people for his treasured possession” (26:16-19).
The people are to set up stones on Mount Ebal, plaster them, and write on them all the words of the law (27:1-8).
Six tribes are to stand on Gerizim for the blessing and six on Ebal for the curse (27:11-14).
The Levites are to recite curses, and all the people say “Amen” (27:15-26).
“And all these blessings shall come upon you and overtake you, if you obey the voice of the LORD your God” (28:2). “The LORD will make you the head and not the tail” (28:13).
interpretation:
The confession in chapter 26 is a brilliant piece of teaching. It tells the whole story of salvation in a few sentences. “A wandering Aramean was my father.” It starts with the humility of Jacob. Then it recalls the slavery, the cry, the rescue, and the gift of the land. And then the worshiper says, “Behold, now I bring the firstfruits of the ground that you, O LORD, have given me.” The offering is a response to the story.

This is how all Christian giving should work. We are not buying God’s favor. We are returning a portion of what he has given because of what he has done. Worship rests on remembering.

The ceremony at Ebal and Gerizim is a dramatic act of covenant renewal. The people are divided on two mountains, with the Levites and the ark in the valley between. Curses are read from one side, blessings from the other. The curses listed in chapter 27 deal with secret sins: idolatry, dishonoring parents, moving boundary markers, taking bribes. After each one, the people say “Amen.” They are agreeing to the consequences. It is a vivid way of saying that no one can say later that he did not know.

The blessings in chapter 28 are expansive. Blessing in the city and in the field, in the womb and the harvest, in coming in and going out. The pattern is of a life under God’s favor that touches everything. Verse 13 says, “The LORD will make you the head and not the tail.” Yet it is conditional: “if you obey.” Everything depends on the heart’s response.

It is important to read this in light of the whole book. Moses has said that Israel was stubborn and that the land was a gift of grace. The blessings are not wages. They are what happens in a life lived within God’s goodness. The tragedy that follows is that Israel does not obey, and the curses fall.
connection: Paul says that Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the law, so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles (Galatians 3:13-14). Ephesians 1:3 says that God “has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places.” The Amen of the people finds its echo in 2 Corinthians 1:20, where all the promises of God find their “Yes” in Christ, and “through him is our Amen.” Revelation 5:14 shows the living creatures saying “Amen.”
application:
Write out your own short account of God’s work in your life, in the pattern of 26:5-10. Say it aloud as a prayer.

Make an offering of thanks, as a response and not as a payment.

Think about the “secret sins” of chapter 27. Is there one that you need to bring into the light?
prayerPrompts: Bring God a portion of what he has given you, and tell him what that is.
Thank him for blessing you in Christ with every spiritual blessing.
Ask him to let your “Amen” be true.
